Series 06 · Blood Sugar

Berberine, Chromium, and Cinnamon: What the Evidence Actually Says

3 May 2026

Walk into any pharmacy and the blood sugar supplement shelf looks full of options. But behind the similar labels are ingredients with dramatically different levels of scientific support. Berberine, chromium, and cinnamon are the three most commonly seen — and the gap between them is significant. Understanding what each one actually does is the difference between a supplement that works and one that doesn't.

Berberine: The One with Real Clinical Data

Berberine is an alkaloid compound found in several plants including barberry, goldenseal, and Oregon grape. It has been studied extensively in human clinical trials — more thoroughly than almost any other natural blood sugar compound. Multiple randomised controlled trials have shown berberine can reduce fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, and postprandial glucose spikes, with effects comparable in some studies to metformin, the most commonly prescribed type 2 diabetes medication.

Its primary mechanism is activation of AMPK (AMP-activated protein kinase) — sometimes called the body's metabolic master switch. This improves insulin sensitivity, reduces hepatic glucose output, slows intestinal absorption of glucose, and enhances cellular uptake. The evidence base is genuinely strong: over 40 human trials, consistent results across independent research groups, and a well-understood mechanism of action.

"Berberine's clinical evidence is unusually robust for a natural compound — it works through the same metabolic pathway as metformin, not around it."

Chromium: Modest Effects in Specific Populations

Chromium is an essential trace mineral involved in insulin signalling — specifically in the function of a molecule called chromodulin, which amplifies insulin's effect on glucose uptake. Studies suggest it may improve glucose tolerance in people who are chromium-deficient, which includes some older adults, people eating highly refined diets, and those with type 2 diabetes. For people with normal chromium status, however, the effect is minimal to non-existent.

This explains the inconsistency in the research: chromium works when there's a deficiency to correct, not as a general blood sugar optimiser. Dosing matters too — most studies showing benefit used 200–1000mcg of chromium picolinate daily, a form with better absorption than chromium chloride.

Cinnamon: Popular, But the Evidence Is Weaker

Cinnamon's reputation in the blood sugar space comes from compounds like cinnamaldehyde and procyanidins, which may slow gastric emptying and reduce the rate of glucose absorption after meals. Some small trials have shown modest reductions in fasting blood glucose — but study quality varies considerably, effect sizes are small, and results frequently disappear when diet is controlled for.

Cinnamon is not harmful at supplement doses, and it pairs well as a flavour component. But it should be viewed as a mild complementary ingredient, not a therapeutic one. A blood sugar formula built primarily around cinnamon is trading on reputation, not evidence.

What to Look for on a Label

A well-formulated blood sugar supplement leads with berberine at a clinically relevant dose — typically 500mg per serving, taken two to three times daily with meals. Chromium picolinate is a reasonable supporting ingredient at 200–400mcg. Cinnamon can appear as a complementary addition. If the label lists cinnamon first and buries berberine in small print, the formulation priorities don't match the evidence. Read the actives and their quantities before the marketing headline.

Series 07 · Omega-3

Omega-3 for Brain & Heart: Why Source and Purity Matter

14 Jun 2026

EPA (eicosapentaenoic acid) and DHA (docosahexaenoic acid) are long-chain omega-3 fatty acids that play critical roles in cardiovascular function, brain health, inflammation regulation, and eye health. Your body cannot synthesise them in meaningful quantities — they must come from diet or supplementation. Yet most people in modern diets are significantly under-consuming both, while over-consuming omega-6 fatty acids from vegetable oils and processed foods.

This imbalance matters. The omega-6 to omega-3 ratio in ancestral diets was estimated around 4:1. In modern Western diets, it's closer to 20:1. That shift drives a chronic low-grade pro-inflammatory state now linked to cardiovascular disease, cognitive decline, metabolic dysfunction, and impaired recovery from exercise.

Molecular Form: The Difference Nobody Talks About

The majority of omega-3 supplements on the market use ethyl ester (EE) form — a processed form created when fatty acids are concentrated and attached to ethanol rather than glycerol. Ethyl esters are cheaper to manufacture, but studies consistently show significantly lower bioavailability than the natural triglyceride (TG) form found in whole fish.

A landmark study published in Prostaglandins, Leukotrienes and Essential Fatty Acids found that triglyceride-form omega-3s absorbed up to 70% more effectively than ethyl ester equivalents under real-world conditions. If your supplement doesn't specify the molecular form on the label, it is almost certainly ethyl ester.

"The form your omega-3 comes in determines how much actually reaches your cells. The same EPA/DHA dose can deliver very different outcomes depending on whether it's bound to glycerol or ethanol."

Oxidation: The Hidden Quality Problem

Omega-3 fatty acids are highly susceptible to oxidation — exposure to heat, light, and oxygen degrades them into aldehydes and other compounds that may be harmful rather than beneficial. Studies of retail fish oil supplements in New Zealand and Australia have found a significant proportion exceed international oxidation thresholds set by the Global Organisation for EPA and DHA (GOED).

Oxidation is invisible in a sealed capsule but detectable: break one open and smell it. A faint, clean ocean scent is acceptable. A strong fishy or rancid smell is oxidation. Quality manufacturers test for peroxide value (PV), anisidine value (AV), and total oxidation (TOTOX), and make those results available. If a brand can't provide oxidation data, that's a meaningful signal.

What EPA and DHA Each Do

EPA and DHA are not interchangeable — they have distinct primary roles. EPA is the dominant anti-inflammatory fatty acid, supporting cardiovascular health and modulating the immune response. DHA is structurally critical for brain and retinal tissue — approximately 40% of the fatty acids in the brain's grey matter are DHA. Both are important, but the ratio matters depending on your health priorities. Most general-purpose supplements target a 2:1 EPA:DHA ratio as a broadly useful starting point.

What to Look for on the Label

A quality omega-3 supplement will state EPA and DHA content per serving as separate figures (not just total "fish oil" content, which can be misleading), specify the molecular form as triglyceride, carry third-party certification such as IFOS (International Fish Oil Standards) or IKOS, and be packaged in an opaque, nitrogen-flushed capsule to minimise oxidation during storage. These specifics separate a therapeutic product from a commodity one.

Series 08 · Standards

Why New Zealand Supplements Are Held to a Higher Standard

28 Jul 2026

When you buy a supplement in New Zealand, you're operating within one of the more rigorous regulatory environments for natural health products in the world. This matters — not because it guarantees every product on the shelf is good, but because the floor for what can be sold here is meaningfully higher than in many other markets, and the compliance requirements create real accountability in the supply chain.

The Regulatory Framework

Natural health products in New Zealand are regulated under the Natural Health and Supplementary Products Act 2023 (NHSP Act), administered by Medsafe. Products must be notified to the New Zealand Natural Health Products Register, carry compliant labelling with permitted claims, and be manufactured to Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) standards. Unlike the United States — where the FDA's pre-market oversight of supplements is minimal and enforcement is largely reactive — New Zealand requires a defined compliance pathway before a product reaches consumers.

GMP certification is audited by recognised bodies including AsureQuality, NSF International, and the TGA (Australia's Therapeutic Goods Administration, which operates under mutual recognition). Certification verifies that a manufacturer's facilities, processes, documentation, and quality systems meet pharmaceutical-grade standards — covering everything from raw ingredient identity testing and contamination controls to batch records, stability data, and finished product release testing.

"In New Zealand, what's on the label has to be in the capsule. That sounds obvious — but it's not the standard everywhere, and the gap between markets is larger than most consumers realise."

What GMP Certification Actually Covers

A GMP-certified manufacturer doesn't simply follow a checklist — the certification represents an independently audited quality system. This means raw ingredients are tested for identity and purity before they enter production. Equipment is validated and calibrated. Manufacturing environments are controlled for temperature, humidity, and contamination. Finished products are tested against their specification before any batch is released for sale. And every step is documented in records that can be audited retrospectively.

The contrast with non-GMP manufacturing is significant. In markets with minimal oversight, studies have repeatedly found supplements that contain less active ingredient than labelled, more of certain compounds than labelled, or contaminants — including heavy metals and undeclared pharmaceutical compounds — not listed anywhere. GMP doesn't eliminate all risk, but it creates systematic accountability that dramatically reduces it.

Third-Party Testing: The Verification Layer

Beyond GMP, quality-focused brands commission independent third-party testing for heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury), microbial contamination, pesticide residues, and active ingredient concentration. This matters because it provides verification outside the manufacturer's own systems — a genuinely independent check on what's in each batch.

Third-party results should be available on request, or ideally published publicly as Certificates of Analysis (COAs). If a brand can't provide this documentation, the gap between what they claim and what's in the product is unverifiable. That's a meaningful quality signal, and it's one of the clearest ways to distinguish a genuinely quality-focused brand from one that's simply well-packaged.

The Questions Worth Asking

When evaluating any supplement, these are the specifics that matter: Is the manufacturer GMP certified, and by which accreditation body? Is there a current Certificate of Analysis for the batch you're buying? Are heavy metal and contaminant results available? These aren't marketing questions — they're quality questions. The brands that answer them clearly are the ones whose products are actually worth taking.

Series 09 · BHB & Ketosis

Ketosis vs. Low-Carb: What’s the Difference and Which Works?

12 Sep 2026

Many people use "low-carb" and "ketosis" interchangeably. They're related — but they describe distinct metabolic states with different physiological effects, and that distinction matters considerably if you're considering BHB supplementation or trying to understand why your low-carb diet may or may not be producing the results you expect.

Low-Carb: A Spectrum, Not a Switch

A low-carbohydrate diet simply reduces carbohydrate intake below a typical Western level. This can range from moderately low — 100–150g of carbs per day — to very low, at 20–50g per day. The metabolic effects vary considerably depending on where on that spectrum you sit, and critically: low-carb eating does not automatically produce ketosis.

Someone eating 100g of carbs daily may feel real benefits — reduced blood sugar spikes, more stable energy, weight loss — but their liver is not in ketogenic mode. They're running a mixed metabolism, using both glucose and some fat for fuel. That's a meaningful improvement over a high-carb diet, but it's not ketosis.

What Ketosis Actually Is

Ketosis is a specific metabolic state: the liver is producing ketone bodies — beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), acetoacetate, and acetone — at a rate sufficient to elevate blood ketone levels above approximately 0.5 mmol/L. This happens when carbohydrate availability drops low enough, and liver glycogen stores deplete enough, that the liver switches its primary output from glucose to ketones derived from fat.

The brain and heart can run efficiently on ketones as an alternative to glucose. During ketosis, the body's reliance on dietary carbohydrate for energy drops substantially — a shift with meaningful implications for appetite regulation, metabolic flexibility, and energy stability.

"Ketosis is not a diet — it's a metabolic state. You can eat low-carb without being in ketosis, and you can be in ketosis without eating perfectly. The liver makes the determination, not the meal plan."

The Threshold That Matters

For most people, sustained nutritional ketosis requires restricting net carbohydrates to under 20–50g per day. But carbohydrate intake is only part of the equation — protein intake matters too. Excess protein can be converted to glucose via gluconeogenesis, which can prevent ketosis even when carbs are very low. Most approaches to therapeutic ketosis target moderate protein intake (around 1.2–1.6g per kg of body weight) alongside minimal carbohydrates.

Individual thresholds vary based on activity level, metabolic health, and body composition. Athletes with high glycogen turnover may maintain ketosis at higher carb intakes than sedentary individuals. Blood ketone testing — using a finger-prick meter — is the only reliable way to confirm you've crossed the threshold; urine strips become unreliable after the first few weeks of adaptation.

Where BHB Supplementation Fits

BHB ketone salts provide exogenous ketones — ketones that come from outside the body rather than from the liver's own fat metabolism. They can transiently raise blood BHB levels regardless of dietary state, which is why they're commonly used to ease the transition into nutritional ketosis, reduce the fatigue and cognitive fog of keto-adaptation (often called "keto flu"), or maintain some ketone availability during periods when strict dietary adherence isn't practical.

Exogenous BHB doesn't replace the deep metabolic adaptation that comes from sustained dietary ketosis — that adaptation, built over weeks, involves mitochondrial changes, enzyme upregulation, and a fundamentally different relationship between fuel availability and energy output. But as a support tool, BHB supplementation bridges gaps, reduces the difficulty of the adaptation window, and extends the flexibility of a ketogenic approach for people maintaining it long-term.

Series 01 · BHB & Weight Management

How BHB Ketone Salts Shift Your Body Into Fat-Burning Mode

25 May 2025

Most weight management supplements chase a single lever — suppress appetite, block fat absorption, or spike metabolism. BHB (Beta-Hydroxybutyrate) works differently. It changes the fundamental fuel source your body prefers to burn, at the cellular level.

What Is BHB?

Beta-Hydroxybutyrate is a ketone body — a molecule your liver produces when carbohydrate availability drops. In a standard diet, your body runs primarily on glucose. When glucose is scarce (through fasting, carbohydrate restriction, or supplementation), your liver ramps up ketone production, and BHB becomes the dominant fuel for your brain, heart, and muscles.

Avenqor's BHB formula delivers exogenous ketone salts, meaning you can begin entering a ketogenic metabolic state without strict dietary deprivation.

"BHB doesn't just tell your body to burn fat — it gives your body a reason to. It's the signal and the fuel, simultaneously."

The Science of Fat Metabolism

When BHB levels rise in the bloodstream, several things happen concurrently:

  • Appetite suppression — BHB suppresses ghrelin, the hunger hormone, reducing caloric intake naturally
  • Fat oxidation — Elevated ketones signal adipose tissue to release stored fatty acids for energy
  • Muscle preservation — Unlike caloric restriction alone, BHB is protein-sparing, protecting lean muscle mass during a deficit
  • Mental clarity — The brain runs exceptionally well on ketones, often resulting in improved focus and reduced brain fog

Why Formulation Matters

Not all BHB products are equal. The mineral salt paired with BHB significantly affects absorption rate and tolerability. Avenqor uses a blend of sodium, magnesium, and calcium BHB salts — optimised for rapid uptake while maintaining electrolyte balance, a common concern with ketogenic diets.

Who Benefits Most?

BHB supplementation is particularly effective for individuals following a low-carbohydrate or ketogenic diet who want to deepen ketosis, those in the early stages of a weight management programme who struggle with energy dips and hunger, and active individuals seeking a clean, sustained energy source without glucose spikes.

As with any supplement, consistency is key. BHB works best as part of a broader lifestyle approach — not as a standalone solution, but as a powerful tool within one.

Series 02 · Blood Sugar Regulation

Why Postprandial Glucose Spikes Matter More Than Fasting Levels

20 Sep 2025

When most people think about blood sugar, they think about fasting glucose — the number on a morning blood test. But emerging research consistently shows that what happens to your blood sugar after a meal is a far more powerful predictor of long-term metabolic health.

The Postprandial Problem

Every time you eat carbohydrates, your blood glucose rises. The speed, height, and duration of that rise — and how quickly your body brings it back to baseline — determines whether your metabolism is functioning optimally or under chronic stress.

A sharp, prolonged spike followed by a steep crash isn't just uncomfortable. Over time, it contributes to insulin resistance, increased fat storage, chronic inflammation, and elevated cardiovascular risk.

"A person can have a 'normal' fasting glucose yet experience dramatic post-meal spikes that, cumulatively, drive metabolic dysfunction over years."

How Avenqor's Formula Works

Our blood sugar support complex targets multiple pathways simultaneously:

  • Berberine — Activates AMPK, the metabolic master switch, improving insulin sensitivity at the cellular level
  • Chromium picolinate — Enhances insulin receptor activity, supporting efficient glucose uptake
  • Cinnamon extract — Slows gastric emptying and inhibits alpha-glucosidase enzymes, flattening the glucose curve after meals
  • Alpha-lipoic acid — A potent antioxidant that reduces oxidative stress caused by glucose fluctuations

The Glucose Curve, Explained

Think of your blood sugar response as a curve on a graph. The goal isn't to eliminate the rise — some rise is natural and necessary. The goal is to keep the peak moderate and the recovery swift. Avenqor's formula is designed to do exactly this: blunt the spike without blocking normal glucose metabolism.

Beyond Diabetes

Blood sugar regulation isn't only relevant to diabetics or pre-diabetics. Even metabolically healthy individuals benefit from stable glucose — better energy levels, reduced cravings, improved sleep quality, and lower long-term disease risk. This formula is designed for anyone who takes their metabolic health seriously.

Series 03 · Sleep Formula

The 2-Phase Sleep Architecture and Why Deep Sleep Is Non-Negotiable

8 Dec 2025

Sleep is not a passive state. It is an active, highly orchestrated biological process — and the quality of that process determines everything from immune function to cognitive performance, body composition, and emotional regulation.

Understanding Sleep Architecture

A full night's sleep consists of multiple 90-minute cycles, each containing two primary phases: Non-REM (NREM) sleep and REM sleep. Within NREM, Stage 3 — also called slow-wave or deep sleep — is where the most critical restoration occurs.

  • Deep sleep (NREM Stage 3) — Physical repair, immune strengthening, growth hormone release, cellular detoxification
  • REM sleep — Memory consolidation, emotional processing, creativity, learning integration

Most adults get far less deep sleep than they need. Stress, blue light exposure, alcohol, and inconsistent sleep schedules all suppress slow-wave sleep — even if total sleep duration appears adequate.

"You can sleep eight hours and still be chronically sleep-deprived — if the architecture is disrupted, the restoration doesn't happen."

How Avenqor Sleep Formula Works

Rather than simply sedating you, our formula works with your body's natural sleep-wake system:

  • Melatonin (low-dose, timed release) — Signals circadian rhythm onset without suppressing natural melatonin production
  • Magnesium glycinate — Activates GABA receptors, reducing neurological arousal and supporting deep sleep onset
  • L-theanine — Promotes alpha brain wave activity, creating calm alertness that transitions into restful sleep
  • Ashwagandha extract (KSM-66®) — Adaptogen that lowers cortisol, the primary antagonist of deep sleep
  • 5-HTP — Precursor to serotonin, supporting healthy sleep-wake neurotransmitter balance

The Cortisol Connection

Elevated evening cortisol is one of the most common — and underappreciated — causes of poor sleep quality. When stress hormones remain high at night, the body resists entering deep sleep stages. Ashwagandha's cortisol-lowering effect addresses the root cause rather than masking the symptom.

What Good Sleep Actually Feels Like

With properly structured sleep, you wake before the alarm feeling genuinely rested — not just "not tired." Cognitive clarity arrives within minutes. Recovery from exercise is faster. Mood is more stable. These aren't aspirational outcomes; they're the normal results of sleep architecture functioning as it should.

Series 04 · High-Purity Fish Oil

Triglyceride vs Ethyl Ester: Which Form of Omega-3 Actually Absorbs?

30 Jan 2026

Walk into any pharmacy and you'll find dozens of fish oil products. Most look similar on the label — EPA and DHA milligrams prominently displayed. But the form of omega-3 inside those capsules varies enormously, and that difference has a profound impact on how much your body actually absorbs.

Two Forms, Very Different Results

Fish oil omega-3s come in two primary molecular forms: triglyceride (TG) and ethyl ester (EE). The distinction matters more than most consumers realise.

  • Triglyceride form — The natural form found in fish. Your body's digestive enzymes (lipases) are specifically designed to process triglycerides. Absorption is efficient, particularly with food.
  • Ethyl ester form — A synthetic, concentrated form created during molecular distillation. Cheaper to produce, but studies consistently show 25–70% lower bioavailability compared to triglyceride form.

"Many consumers are paying for omega-3s that their body cannot efficiently use. The label shows the dose — not the absorption."

The New Zealand Advantage

Avenqor sources its fish oil from deep, cold New Zealand and sub-Antarctic waters — among the most pristine marine environments on Earth. The cold water fish (predominantly hoki and tuna) naturally accumulate higher concentrations of EPA and DHA, and the remote sourcing location means significantly lower heavy metal and environmental contaminant exposure.

Every batch is third-party tested for:

  • Mercury, lead, cadmium, and arsenic
  • PCBs and dioxins
  • Oxidation levels (TOTOX value) — a measure of freshness that most brands don't disclose

Why Freshness Matters

Oxidised fish oil is not just ineffective — it may be actively harmful. Rancid omega-3s generate free radicals that contribute to the very inflammation you're trying to reduce. The "fishy burp" commonly associated with fish oil supplements is almost always a sign of oxidation. Avenqor's product is manufactured and encapsulated in an oxygen-minimised environment, and nitrogen-flushed before sealing.

Recommended Use

Take with the largest meal of the day for optimal absorption. Fat-soluble compounds are absorbed in the context of dietary fats — taking fish oil on an empty stomach significantly reduces uptake regardless of the form.

Series 05 · Krill Oil

How Phospholipid Omega-3s from Krill Reach Cells Fish Oil Cannot

17 Mar 2026

Krill oil and fish oil both deliver EPA and DHA — the two omega-3 fatty acids most associated with cardiovascular, cognitive, and anti-inflammatory benefits. But the way they deliver these fatty acids is fundamentally different, and that difference changes what your cells actually receive.

The Phospholipid Advantage

In fish oil, omega-3s are packaged as triglycerides. In krill oil, they're packaged as phospholipids — the same molecular structure that forms the membrane of every cell in your body.

This isn't a minor detail. Cell membranes are selectively permeable — they control what enters and exits the cell with extraordinary precision. Phospholipid-bound omega-3s are recognised and incorporated far more readily than triglyceride-bound ones, because they speak the same molecular language as the membrane itself.

"Think of phospholipid omega-3s as having a universal key to your cell membranes. Triglyceride omega-3s have to knock and wait."

Astaxanthin: Krill's Built-In Antioxidant

Antarctic krill naturally contain astaxanthin — one of the most potent antioxidants found in nature, responsible for krill's characteristic pink-red colour. This matters for omega-3 supplementation because:

  • Omega-3 fatty acids are highly susceptible to oxidation
  • Astaxanthin acts as an in-built preservative, protecting the EPA and DHA within the same capsule
  • Astaxanthin itself has independently studied benefits for skin health, exercise recovery, and eye health

No Fishy Aftertaste — and Why

The absence of fish oil's characteristic aftertaste in krill oil isn't just about palatability. It's a marker of oxidation status. Krill oil's natural antioxidant content keeps the fatty acids stable. If your omega-3 supplement has a strong fishy smell or taste, that's oxidation — and oxidised fats counteract the very benefits you're supplementing for.

Sustainability

Antarctic krill represent one of the largest biomasses on Earth and are harvested under some of the world's strictest fishery management regulations. Avenqor sources exclusively from Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) certified fisheries, ensuring that every capsule supports — rather than undermines — the ocean ecosystem it comes from.

Fish Oil vs Krill Oil: Which Should You Choose?

For most people, krill oil offers superior cellular uptake and comes with the added benefit of astaxanthin. For those requiring very high doses of EPA/DHA (such as therapeutic cardiovascular doses of 3–4g daily), high-concentration fish oil may be more economical. Both have a place — and Avenqor offers both, to the same standard of purity and integrity.
